source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:41 ('ברכו — the resh with sheva ALONE, as our custom')
claim_en: THE HALF-VOWEL LAW, STATION 8 IN ITS OWN SPAN: ברכו ('[the blessing with which his father] BLESSED HIM', 27:41) — Minchat Shai rules the resh with plain sheva (the bare half-vowel) 'as our custom'; SNAPSHOT points hataf patach (the compound half-vowel) — the eighth station of the resh-class split, censused from gen_46's span, now source-anchored inside its own unit. DISCREPANCY observation; both camps recorded.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:41 ('ואהרגה — the vav in sheva and the aleph in patach; Chizkuni')
claim_en: THE KILL-COHORTATIVE POINTED AS RULED: ואהרגה ('that I may KILL [my brother]') — the vav in sheva (the half-vowel) and the aleph in patach (the short a) exactly as Minchat Shai cites from the Chizkuni; SNAPSHOT letter-identical, meteg (the small stress-stroke) on the aleph.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:46 ('בחיי — the bet soft')
claim_en: THE SOFT BET OF THE WEARY LIFE: בחיי ('I am disgusted WITH MY LIFE' — Rebecca's pressure-speech) — the bet soft (no dagesh, the doubling dot) as Minchat Shai rules; the pattern bet-then-sheva with nothing between is the absence proof on SNAPSHOT's own string.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:46 ('קצתי — small qof; see Rabbeinu Bachya') + Kitzur Baal HaTurim on 27:46 (the qof of one hundred: the House a hundred cubits high destined for ruin; the LARGE qof of the sparrow's nest, Ps 84, David's plea that it stand)
claim_en: THE SMALL QOF (manual): קצתי ('I am DISGUSTED', 27:46) is written with a small qof per the scribal lists — the letter-size layer is uninstrumented on SNAPSHOT (standing gap; the token itself verified present at 27:46).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 28:5 ('את יעקב — the qof in zaqef qatan and the bet with no pashta')
claim_en: THE SEND-OFF ACCENT AS RULED: יעקב in 'and Isaac SENT JACOB away' (28:5) carries zaqef qatan (the small upright pause-accent) and no pashta (the forward-leaning accent) — SNAPSHOT letter-identical with Minchat Shai's ruling, the sliced pattern doubling as the absence proof.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 28:6 ('וירא עשו — with revia')
claim_en: THE FIRST SEEING RESTS ON A DOT: עשו in 'and Esau SAW that Isaac had blessed Jacob' (28:6) carries revia (the resting dot-accent) as Minchat Shai rules — the pause sits on the seer's own name.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 28:6 ('בברכו — the bet with wide qamatz and with the lengthening stroke in ALL the books; the resh with sheva alone in SOME of them, and in some with sheva-patach — I wrote of this at the head of Lech Lecha')
claim_en: THE LAW'S FIRST SPLIT-ATTESTED STATION: בברכו ('WHEN HE BLESSED him', 28:6) — Minchat Shai himself records the books DIVIDED on the resh: sheva alone in some, sheva-patach (hataf) in others. SNAPSHOT points hataf patach — joining the compound camp, consistent with all eight censused resh stations: the tradition's own division is external witness that the class is real. Sub-variance: the root-bet carries qamatz but NO meteg (the lengthening stroke MS reports in all books) — meteg-omission class.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 28:9 ('את — with maqqef')
claim_en: THE JOINED OBJECT-WORD: את before מחלת ('and he took MAHALATH', 28:9) carries the maqqef (the joining stroke) as Minchat Shai rules — SNAPSHOT stores the join on the token itself.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 28:9 ('מחלת — in the precise books and the early print the mem in qamatz, so Or Torah; the chet in sheva-patach in ALL the books — the printer who set plain sheva was already refuted by Or Torah')
claim_en: THE PRECISE BOOKS WIN AT MAHALATH: מחלת (Esau's Ishmaelite bride, a Torah one-time name) — mem in qamatz and chet in hataf patach exactly as the precise books and Or Torah rule; SNAPSHOT arbitrates AGAINST the printer's plain sheva. (The guttural chet takes the compound half-vowel by nature — the inverse shape of the resh-class split.)

A NARRATIVE GAP IS FILLED BY A DOCTRINE, AND THAT DOCTRINE IS WHAT THE TRANSLATION ALREADY WROTE. 'It was told to Rebecca' names no teller, and the chain answers that the matriarchs were prophets and she among them, with the furrow-in-furrow argument - a prophet does not plow a furrow into a furrow, so her plan carried foreknowledge. This is the source row for the doctrine Onkelos plants inside 27:13 in gen_46: the licence written into that verse is stated outright here, two blocks apart and in the opposite order.

check.note: A doctrine stated at this verse that the translation had already written into an earlier verse in another block.

claim_en: THE HINGE WORD OF THE BLOCK IS READ TWO INCOMPATIBLE WAYS. The chain reads that he consoles himself as the cup of consolation ALREADY DRUNK - the killing settled in his mind, mourning taken in advance. Onkelos renders the same word as LIES IN WAIT FOR YOU, concrete ambush. One member reads an interior resolution, the other an external posture, on the word that turns the block.

check.note: The block's hinge word read as an interior state by one member and a physical ambush by the other.

claim_en: A VAGUE PHRASE IS MADE A TERM OF YEARS BY VERBAL ANALOGY. 'A few days' here is equated with the same phrase at 29:20, where seven years seemed like a few days - and the inference is drawn: as there seven years, so here seven years. The mother's imprecision becomes the exile's first clock by an explicit analogy between two occurrences of one word. The chain then holds her 'until his anger subsides' against a prophet's ink that the wrath was kept forever, and records that the subsiding never came.

check.note: An indefinite phrase given a numeric value by verbal analogy with its other occurrence, then contradicted from a later book.

claim_en: THE UNTOLD YEARS BETWEEN TWO VERSES ARE COUNTED. Sixty-three at the blessing, taken from the arithmetic on Ishmael's years recorded at gen_42, plus FOURTEEN YEARS HIDDEN IN THE HOUSE OF EVER between these verses, plus seven worked, gives eighty-four at the marriage - with the principle stated: He delays for the righteous and advances the wicked, the brother having married at forty. A gap in the narrative is filled with a determinate number and the number is used.

check.note: A narrative gap assigned a specific duration, chained to an arithmetic recorded in an earlier block.

claim_en: A LATER CONTRACT IS READ AS DRAFTED AGAINST THIS FAMILY'S RECORD. 'I will work for RACHEL, YOUR DAUGHTER, THE YOUNGER' is read as three deliberate specifications, because the townsmen are deceivers: not the other sister, not some other woman of the same name, no substitution by renaming. The charlatan reading of 25:20, chartered at gen_43, cashes here as anti-fraud drafting - and the chain adds that even in a carpenter's vise the wicked avails you nothing.

check.note: Contract terms read as anti-fraud specifications answering a character dossier built in an earlier block.

claim_en: THE PLOT IS DECODED IN FULL AND ENROLLED IN A CENSUS OF INTERIOR PLOTS. From 'Esau said IN HIS HEART' the chain reconstructs the calculus: Cain killed his brother and the father lived on and begot heirs - therefore I will kill my father first, then my brother, and inherit alone; 'let the days of mourning approach' read as let me hasten them. The verse is then counted as one of three who plotted in the heart and failed, and enrolled in the standing rule that the wicked are ruled BY their hearts while the righteous rule theirs.

check.note: An interior monologue reconstructed as a full plan and classed into a corpus-wide census of heart-plots.

claim_en: THE GRUDGE VERB IS EXPANDED INTO THE EMPIRE'S OWN TITLE. R. Elazar bar R. Yosei reads the verb for bearing a grudge as an acronym - hater, avenger, grudge-bearer - and adds that to this day they are called by that name as the senators of Rome. A single narrative verb converted into a standing designation for a political body.

check.note: A narrative verb read as an acronym and applied as a title to a contemporary institution.

claim_en: THE SAME VERSE THAT CARRIES THE MURDER PLAN ALSO CARRIES A MERIT. Among three merits feared on Esau's account, the chain counts his waiting for the days of mourning - reading the very restraint that delays the killing as filial honour. Alongside it the later fear is split across two verbs, frightened lest he kill and distressed lest he be killed, and the rule is stated that no promise to the righteous holds unconditionally in this world.

check.note: One clause read simultaneously as a murder plan and as evidence of filial honour.

claim_en: THE RATIFICATION MAXIM TAKES ITS HOME SEAT AT THE SUMMONS. The blessings are held uncertain in his hand until this verse, where he summoned and blessed knowingly - and R. Elazar's maxim is stated at its own seat: ratification of a document is only by its signatories, lest you say that without the deceit he would not have been blessed. The parable of the king's son digging follows: why clandestinely - take it openly. The maxim stated in gen_46 is anchored here.

check.note: A document-ratification maxim reaching its home verse, retroactively validating an earlier act.

claim_en: THE TRANSLATION NATIONALIZES THE BLESSING AND REGULARIZES THE OBEDIENCE. An assembly of peoples becomes an assembly of TRIBES, the third seat in this parashah of the policy that converts general terms into national ones. And 'heeded his father and his mother' becomes ACCEPTED FROM them, the obedience verb absorbed into the standing acceptance vocabulary the buffer uses for hearing throughout.

check.note: A general term nationalized and an obedience verb standardized into the translation's acceptance register.

claim_en: A STANDING STRATEGIC TABLE IS BUILT OVER THE WHOLE EXILE. Each tribe is paired against a kingdom with the matching figure and its named slayer - lion against lion, wolf against wolf with an ink claim on the written-and-read forms, the third tribe against the third kingdom with three letters each, and horns against horns - closing on the tradition that Esau falls only into the hands of Rachel's descendants. A whole-corpus adversarial table hung on this block's grudge.

check.note: A tribe-against-kingdom pairing table spanning the corpus, each pair carrying its own figure and named agent.

claim_en: THE CANON'S BLESSINGS ARE SPLICED INTO A CHAIN, AND THIS VERSE IS THE FIRST LINK. The relay rule is stated: where one concluded, the next begins. Isaac ended at the summons-blessing of 28:1-3; Jacob began his blessing with a summons and ended with 'this'; Moses began with 'this is the blessing' and ended at happy-are-you; David began at happy-is-the-man. The chain formally splices four blessings across three books into one sequence, and our verse opens it.

check.note: Four blessings across three books spliced end-to-start into a single chain beginning at this verse.
